title: Proper direct image of bounded-below ind-constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $p\colon X\to Y$ proper with geometric fibres of dimension $\leq d$, and
$K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ bounded below. Then $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)\in\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$ for all $n$; if $K$
has cohomology in degrees $\geq a$ then so does $Rp_*K$; and if $K$ has cohomology in degrees $\leq b$
then $Rp_*K$ has cohomology in degrees $\leq b+2d+1$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A_Z=\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$ for $Z=X,Y$. The module-object action is equivalently a sheafwise ring-module action: by the universal property of the sheaf tensor product, a map $\Lambda_Z\otimes M\to M$ is a bilinear sheaf action, with the same unit and associativity equations. Thus the ringed-site Grothendieck theorem [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] applies to these categories. The functor $p_*$ is additive and left exact by [def-sfb-module-lower-star], and $Rp_*$ is computed on K-injective resolutions in this very module category by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Choose $a_0\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^v(K)=0$ for $v<a_0$; canonical truncation below $a_0$ replaces a representative of K by a quasi-isomorphic bounded-below complex. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to obtain $E_2^{u,v}=R^up_*\mathcal H^v(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{u+v}(Rp_*K)$, supported in $u\geq0$, $v\geq a_0$. Parts (5) and (6) give a finite exhaustive separated decreasing filtration $F^u\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)$, with $F^0=\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)$, $F^u=0$ for sufficiently large u, and $F^u/F^{u+1}\cong E_\infty^{u,n-u}$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: the hypercohomology spectral sequence and its finite abutment filtration

proof.text: For every v, the sheaf $\mathcal H^v(K)$ lies in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ because K is an object of $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$. Applying [sk-lem-proper-heart-bound] to this sheaf gives $E_2^{u,v}=R^up_*\mathcal H^v(K)=0$ for $u>2d+1$ and places every nonzero $E_2^{u,v}$ in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: application of sk-lem-proper-heart-bound to the E2-page

proof.text: Set $c=2d+1$. Starting with the E2-page of Step 2, induct on $r\geq2$. By [def-sp-exact-couple] the next page is $E_{r+1}^{u,v}=\ker(d_r^{u,v})/\operatorname{im}(d_r^{u-r,v+r-1})$, and the incoming image lies in the outgoing kernel because $d_r^2=0$. For a differential $f:A\to B$ between page terms, [det-ind-heart-kernels-cokernels] puts $\ker f$ and $\coker f$ in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$; then $\operatorname{im}f=\ker(B\to\coker f)$ lies there too. Apply the same closure to the map from the incoming image into the outgoing kernel: its cokernel is $E_{r+1}^{u,v}$, hence is ind-constructible. This also shows that a zero page position stays zero, so every page is supported in $0\leq u\leq c$. Since $d_r$ has bidegree $(r,1-r)$ by [thm-sp-truncation-e2], when $r>c$ every differential between these columns has zero source or zero target. Choose an integer $R\geq2$ with $R>c$. All pages from R onward coincide; thus $E_\infty^{u,v}=E_R^{u,v}$ is ind-constructible by the finite induction, including when the column interval is empty.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: passage from E2 to Er and E-infinity by kernels and cokernels

proof.text: For fixed n, use the finite decreasing filtration of Step 1. Its graded pieces $E_\infty^{u,n-u}$ are ind-constructible by Step 3; those outside $0\leq u\leq2d+1$ are zero. Start with $F^N=0$ for sufficiently large N, which is ind-constructible since the zero sheaf is constructible. For each $u=N-1,\ldots,0$ the short exact sequence $0\to F^{u+1}\to F^u\to E_\infty^{u,n-u}\to0$ has ind-constructible left and right terms. Apply [det-ind-heart-extensions] at each of these finitely many steps. It follows that $F^0=\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)$ lies in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: finite filtration and closure under extensions

proof.text: If $\mathcal H^v(K)=0$ for $v<a$ and $n<a$, then any position $u+v=n$ with $u\geq0$ has $v\leq n<a$, so its E2-term is zero. Page recursion preserves this zero, and all graded pieces of the finite filtration of $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)$ vanish. Descending through that filtration gives $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)=0$. If instead $\mathcal H^v(K)=0$ for $v>b$ and $n>b+2d+1$, then in each possible column $0\leq u\leq2d+1$ one has $v=n-u>b$, while all remaining columns are zero by Step 2. Thus all E2-terms of total degree n are zero, all corresponding stable terms are zero, and every successive quotient in the finite abutment filtration is zero. Starting at its zero end and descending to $F^0$ gives $\mathcal H^n(Rp_*K)=0$.
